items.text: The Imbolc Fire Festival is thousands of years old and began in the village of Marsden, England. People come to this festival to celebrate the arrival of Spring and the end of Winter as the festival happens halfway between the Winter Solstice and the Spring Equinox . This year, thousands of spectators came to see the torch-lit procession of people in druid costumes. The festival organiser said that this year there are two giants in the festival with one representing Winter as Jack Frost and the other representing Spring as the Green Man . A battle happens between them and the Green Man wins since Spring is beginning. Difficult words: Winter Solstice (the shortest possible day of the year), Spring Equinox (when the day and night are of equal lengths), procession (a parade), druid (a priest or a magician from the ancient Celtic religion, or a present-day person who believes in this religion), Jack Frost (a personification of Winter), Green Man (a personification of the forest and plant growth). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In a village in England, the Imbolc Fire Festival began thousands of years ago. People come to this festival to celebrate the beginning of Spring and the end of Winter as the festival happens halfway between the Winter Solstice and the Spring Equinox . This year, thousands of people came to the parade to see people with torches in druid costumes. The festival organiser said that there are two giants representing Winter and Spring in the festival this year. They have a battle which Spring wins. Difficult words: Winter Solstice (the shortest day of the year), Spring Equinox (when the day and night are equally long), druid (a person from the old Celtic religion, or a present-day person who believes in this religion). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is a village in England. It has a festival that is thousands of years old. It is called the Imbolc Fire Festival. It celebrates the beginning of Spring and the end of Winter. This year, thousands of spectators come to the festival. They want to see the procession . People carry torches and wear Druid costumes . The festival organiser says that the procession has two giants in it this year. The giants are supposed to be Winter and Spring. They have a battle. Spring wins. Difficult words: spectator (a person who watches an event), procession (a large group of people moving together), Druid costume (clothing of a person from an old religion of the United Kingdom), giant (a very big person). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This year, the Super Bowl, NFL’s annual fixture , went north to Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA. The Super Bowl was the coldest ever on record and people played it indoors, as temperatures were -17 degrees Celsius or 1 degree Fahrenheit. Thousands of Eagles and Patriots fans were in the city and many activities were outdoors despite the cold. One man explained that people need to try to enjoy being outside so that the cold will not bother them so much. An ice sculpture artist said that he thinks that the cold weather is beautiful but that the city needs more snow. Difficult words: annual (happening every year), fixture (a thing that regularly happens). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

This year, the Super Bowl went north to Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA. It was the coldest Super Bowl ever on record. People played it indoors, as the temperatures were -17 degrees Celsius or 1 degree Fahrenheit. Thousands of fans were in the city and many activities were outside despite the cold. One man explained that people have to try to enjoy being outside so that the cold does not seem so bad. An ice sculpture artist said that the weather was beautiful but that the city needs more snow. Difficult words: Super Bowl (an American football game that happens once a year where two teams compete to be the best). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This year, the Super Bowl goes to Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA. This Super Bowl is the coldest ever. People have to play the game inside. Temperatures are -17 degrees Celsius or 1 degree Fahrenheit. Thousands of fans are visiting. Many activities are still outside. One man says that it is good to enjoy being outside. Then the cold does not feel so bad. An ice artist says that the weather is beautiful. However, he thinks that the city needs more snow. Difficult words: Super Bowl (an American football game that happens once a year where two teams compete to be the best), need (when it is good to have something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A Japanese military helicopter crashed in south-western Japan, ripping off the top floor of a house and setting it on fire. The Japanese Defence Ministry said that it does not know if there have been any deaths, but local media reported that there were two people on board the combat helicopter at the time of the incident . Difficult words: combat (related to the military and to fighting), incident (a memorable event). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A Japanese military helicopter crashed in south-western Japan. It ripped off the top floor of a house and set it on fire. The Japanese Defence Ministry said that it does not know if anyone died. The Japanese media said that there were two people in the helicopter when it crashed. Difficult words: military (the people who fight for a country), rip off (destroy with a lot of force), Defence Ministry (the organisation that works with the people who defend and fight for a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A helicopter crashes in south-western Japan. It is a military helicopter. It crashes into a house. It destroys the top floor. It sets the house on fire. The Japanese Defence Ministry says that it does not know if people died. The Japanese media says that there are two people in the helicopter when it crashes. Difficult words: military (the people who fight for a country), destroy (break completely), Defence Ministry (army), media (television, radio, newspapers). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

07-02-18 15:00 The supermarket chain called Intermarche dropped the price of Nutella by 70%; a 950-gramme jar’s price dropped from 4.50 Euros to 1.41 Euros. Nutella is a popular chocolate spread and the price drop made some people nuts in France. There were brawls in the supermarkets and police had to come to some stores to stop the fighting. The producer of Nutella, Ferrero, said that the decision to drop the price was unilaterally decided by Intermarche. Difficult words: make nuts (make crazy for), brawl (a fight), unilateral (decide only by one group or person). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

07-02-18 15:00 A supermarket chain dropped the price of Nutella by 70%. A 950-gramme jar’s price dropped from 4.50 Euros to 1.41 Euros. Nutella is a popular chocolate spread and the drop in price made some French people nuts . Police had to come break up fights over the product in supermarkets. The maker of Nutella said that it was the supermarket chain that decided to drop the price. Difficult words: chain (many small businesses of the same name and business), make nuts (make crazy for), decide (think about and make or do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

07-02-18 15:00 A supermarket chain drops the price of a popular food. The food is called Nutella. It is a chocolate spread. Nutella gets 70% cheaper. A jar of it goes from 4.50 Euros to 1.41 Euros. This makes some French people nuts . They fight in the stores . Police have to come stop them. Difficult words: chain (many small businesses of the same name and business), make nuts (make crazy for), store (a shop). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Lego, the famous building block, is celebrating its 60 th anniversary. In 1934, Ole Kirk Kristiansen named ‘Lego’ after two Danish words, ‘Leg Godt’, that mean ‘play well’. In 1958, the Lego brick as we recognise it today became patented . The company says that now there are 915,103,765 ways to work with the two-dot-by-four-dot brick ! The company often works with film franchises to update the toy for different times. It also has theme parks around the world of famous places made out of Lego. Difficult words: patent (when the government gives a right to a company to be the only one to make something for a certain time), two-dot-by-four-dot brick (the rectangular brick with eight dots on it), film franchise (a set of movies about a story like ‘Harry Potter’ or ‘Star Wars’). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Lego is celebrating its 60 th anniversary. In 1934, its creator named ‘Lego’ after two Danish words which mean ‘play well’. In 1958, the Lego brick as we know it became patented . The company says that now you can play with the dotted brick in 915,103,765 ways! The company also works with film companies to keep the toy interesting for changing times. In addition, there are theme parks around the world of famous places made out of Lego. Difficult words: patent (when the government says that a company can be the only one to make something for a certain time), dotted (with little circles), brick (one Lego piece). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 1934, a Danish man makes Lego bricks . He names them ‘Lego’ after two Danish words. The words mean ‘play well’. In 1958, people patent Lego bricks. Now the company is 60 years old. Now it says that you can play with one of its bricks in 915,103,765 ways! The company also works with film businesses. It wants to keep the toy interesting. In addition, Lego has theme parks . The parks are around the world. They show famous places made out of the toys. Difficult words: Lego brick (a small toy brick that you can use to build things), patent (when the government says that a company can be the only one to make something for some time), theme park (parks like Legoland or Disneyland). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In central Peru, potato farmers are trying to cope with market prices well below the production by protesting for the government to buy their crops. Police used tear gas and truncheons on the protesters who responded by throwing rocks. Dozens of people have been injured and two people died in the widespread unrest . In other parts of the country, farmers blocked roads and attempted to occupy a hydroelectric dam. Difficult words: cope (deal with, survive), truncheon (a short, thick stick carried as a weapon), dozens (many), unrest (protests or violence), attempt (try). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Peru, the market price of potatoes is well below production costs, and potato farmers are protesting to the government to buy their crops. Police used tear gas and truncheons on the protesters who responded by throwing rocks. Many people were injured and two people died. In other parts of the country, farmers blocked roads and tried to occupy a hydroelectric dam . Difficult words: tear gas (gas which hurts your eyes), truncheon (a short, thick stick carried as a weapon), hydroelectric dam (a barrier which holds water in a lake – water going through produces electricity). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Peru, the price of potatoes is low. Farmers there have problems. They want the government ’s help. They protest. Police use tear gas and truncheons . The protesters throw rocks. Many people are injured. Two people die. The protesters also block roads. Difficult words: government (the ‘bosses’ of a country), tear gas (gas which hurts your eyes), truncheon (a short, thick stick). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists in China successfully cloned two healthy monkeys using the same cloning method used to produce Dolly the sheep. In the past, Dolly rose to fame for being the first mammal to be cloned from an adult animal. The macaques are the first primates to be cloned, which is an important breakthrough as monkeys are closely related to humans. The researchers say that the goal is to clone monkeys for medical research with their main focus initially being on Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases. Difficult words: macaque (a medium-sized monkey). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Scientists in China successfully cloned two healthy monkeys using the same method which produced Dolly the sheep. Dolly was famous because she was the first cloned mammal . The monkeys are the first cloned primates , and this is an important moment because primates are more similar to humans. Scientists say that they want to clone monkeys for medical research to study Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases. Difficult words: mammal (an animal whose babies drink their mother’s milk and have fur and warm blood), primate (a mammal like a monkey or human), research (doing science). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Dolly is a sheep. People clone her in 1996. She is the first cloned mammal . This is an important moment. Scientists in China now clone monkeys. Monkeys are more like humans. This is another important moment. The scientists want to clone monkeys. They want to study Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases. Difficult words: clone (make an animal which is exactly the same as another animal), mammal (an animal whose babies drink their mother’s milk). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On January 26th, Australians marked Australia Day with both celebrations and protests as the day commemorates the arrival of the British First Fleet in Sydney in 1788. Nationwide celebrations included parades, Aboriginal dances and citizenship ceremonies . On the other hand, many people dub 26th January as Invasion Day, due to the effect of settlement on indigenous Australians. Tens of thousands of people attended a rally in Melbourne, calling for equal rights for Aboriginal people. Difficult words: Aboriginal (of the Aboriginal people – the people who were already living in Australia when the Europeans came), citizenship ceremonies (the final step of becoming an Australian citizen), dub (call), indigenous (original to a place), rally (a protest). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Australia Day is on January 26 th which is the day when the British came to Sydney in 1788. Australians held both celebrations and protests with parades , Aboriginal dances and citizenship ceremonies, which are the final step of becoming an Australian citizen. On the other hand, many people call 26th January Invasion Day. Tens of thousands of people met in Melbourne where they protested for equal rights for Aboriginal people. Difficult words: parade (an event when people walk in the street to celebrate something), Aboriginal (related to the Aboriginal people – the people who were already living in Australia when the Europeans came), equal rights (if people have equal rights, they can do same things, have the same protection and respect). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 1788, the British come to Australia. This is on 26th January. There are people already in Australia. They are the Aboriginal people . People now call this day Australia Day. They celebrate. They have special events, parades and dancing. Not everybody likes the day, however. Some people call it Invasion Day. Difficult words: Aboriginal people (the people who are in Australia before the British come), parade (an event when people walk in the street to celebrate something), invasion (when a people take over a place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Near Oklahoma, USA, an oil rig exploded and five people are missing from 20 people that were working in the area at the time of the explosion. It happened on Monday morning, yet the flames were still going by midday. Authorities from the Oklahoma Office of Emergency Management said that it was unclear if there were fatalities . Difficult words: fatality (a death). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Near Oklahoma, USA, an oil rig exploded in the morning. By midday, the oil rig was still on fire. Twenty people were working in the area when the oil rig exploded, and five people are still missing. Officials from the Oklahoma Office of Emergency Management said that it was unclear if there were fatalities . Difficult words: oil rig (a large machine that digs deep in the earth to pull up oil), Office of Emergency Management (a part of the government that works to prevent and help with emergencies), unclear (not known), fatality (a death). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Near Oklahoma, USA, an oil rig explodes. Twenty people are working around the oil rig. Five people are still missing. The explosion happens in the morning. There is a big fire. It keeps burning in the afternoon. Officers are investigating the incident . They do not know if there are any deaths. Difficult words: oil rig (a big machine that digs for oil), officer (someone in a position of authority – a police officer, for example), incident (a very good or a very bad situation), investigate (find out about something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the Philippines, there were billows of smoke and ash coming out from Mount Mayon, so the country issued a level four alert, which meant that a moderate eruption would happen. Once the volcano erupted, red-hot lava spewed out and reached up past 700 metres. Over 40,000 villagers evacuated to shelters . One woman said that she heard people screaming and she looked out at the volcano, where she saw thick smoke coming down. She said that everyone was shouting and looking for their children to be able to evacuate. The volcano has erupted 47 times and caused deadly mud flows and ash falls . Difficult words: billow (a large mass of something, such as a cloud or smoke), spew out (fly out into the air), shelter (a safe place), mud flow (a landslide), ash fall (when ash falls down and makes it difficult for people to breathe). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In the Philippines, smoke and ash were coming out from a volcano. The government alerted people that a large eruption would happen. Once the volcano erupted, lava spewed out and reached up over 700 metres. Over 40,000 villagers had to evacuate. One woman said that she looked out at the volcano, and saw thick smoke coming down. People were shouting and looking for their children to be able to evacuate. The volcano has erupted 47 times, caused deadly landslides and ash falls . Difficult words: alert (tell about a danger), spew out (fly into the air), ash fall (when ash falls down and makes it difficult for people to breathe; ash is a very thick smoke). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the Philippines, there is a volcano. It erupts 47 times. It can move land. It can make the air difficult to breathe. Recently, there are smoke and ash coming out of this volcano. The country alerts people. It says that a big eruption can happen. The volcano erupts. Very hot lava flies out of the volcano. It flies 700 metres into the air. Over 40,000 villagers evacuate . Difficult words: ash (a very thick smoke), alert (tell about a danger), lava (rock that is so hot it turns into liquid), evacuate (go away to be safe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Turkey launched airstrikes on Afrin, a district and a city in the north of Syria, on Saturday to drive out Kurdish fighters from the region. After four days of fighting, Turkish soldiers moved into the Kurdish enclave . Turkish officials want to create a 30-kilometres ‘safe zone’ around the Afrin district. Turkey says that the YPG is an outlawed Kurdish rebel group that is fighting inside its borders. Turkey’s operation is called ‘Operation Olive Branch’ and it raised tensions with the USA. Difficult words: launch (start), district (an area of a country), enclave (a smaller area which is surrounded by a bigger area; people in the small area are in some way different from the people in the big area), raise tensions (make a situation between people or countries worse). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Afrin is a region and a city in the north of Syria. It is also a Kurdish enclave . Turkey launched airstrikes on the region last Saturday, as it wanted to drive out the Kurdish fighters from the region. After four days of fighting, Turkish soldiers moved into the Kurdish enclave. Turkey wants to create a 30-kilometres ‘safe zone’ around Afrin. This turns the relations between Turkey and the USA worse. Difficult words: enclave (a smaller area a bigger area surrounds; people in the small area are in some way different from the people in the big area), launch (start), airstrike (an attack from an airplane). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Afrin is a region and a city in the north of Syria. It is also a Kurdish enclave . Turkish planes bomb the region. Turkey wants to drive out the Kurdish fighters. After four days, Turkish soldiers move into the enclave. Turkey wants to create a 30-kilometres ‘safe zone’ around Afrin. This makes relations between Turkey and the USA worse. Difficult words: enclave (a small area which a big area surrounds; people in the small area are in some way different from the people in the big area), drive out (make go away), relations (the ‘feelings’ between two countries). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Workers were fixing the drainage along a bridge that they were building when the structure fell. There were 21 people at the site at the moment of the incident, ten of which died. Authorities are trying to determine if anyone is missing. Difficult words: drainage (a system of drains – pipes for rain or waste water), structure (building), determine (find out). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Workers were working on a bridge in Colombia when it fell. There were 21 people at the site at the moment of the incident . Ten people died. Authorities are trying to find out if anyone is missing. Difficult words: site (the place of the bridge), incident (a situation when something memorable happens), authorities (somebody in a position of authority – the police, for example). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People are building a bridge in Colombia. There are 21 workers at the bridge. The bridge falls down. Ten people die. Authorities try to find out if more people are missing . Difficult words: authorities (somebody in a position of authority or who is a leader – the police, for example), find out (to get information about something), be missing (if you are missing, people do not know where you are and if you are OK). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An 80-year-old pensioner from England passed her 55-minute Grade 7 ballet exam with merit . Barbara began ballet at the age of two, and while she stopped taking exams in her twenties, she never stopped teaching ballet. She says that it has kept her healthy. Barbara’s daughter, who began taking adult ballet classes, recently persuaded her to start taking exams again. To prepare, she had to train two hours every day for three weeks. Although Barbara lost her flexibility, and she has not done the splits for ten years, she plans to keep on dancing and has her sights on her Grade 8 ballet exams. Difficult words: merit (with around 60%–70% of points), persuade (talk to somebody and force or convince him or her to do something), the splits (putting your legs apart completely). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Barbara from England began ballet at the age of two. She stopped taking exams when she was in her twenties, but she never stopped teaching ballet. She says that it has kept her healthy. Barbara is 80 years old now. Her daughter began taking adult ballet classes and persuaded Barbara to start taking the exams again. Barbara trained two hours every day for three weeks and then passed her Grade 7 ballet exams. She plans to keep on dancing and take the Grade 8 exams. Difficult words: persuade (talk to somebody and convince him or her do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A girl starts ballet when she is two. Her name is Barbara. She is from England. She stops taking exams when she is around 20. She teaches ballet, however. Many years later, the girl grows into an old woman. She is 80 years old now. Her daughter starts ballet. Her daughter persuades Barbara to start taking exams again. Barbara trains two hours every day for three weeks. She takes Grade 7 ballet exams. She passes. Her plan is to keep dancing. She plans to take Grade 8 exams, too. Difficult words: exam (a formal test), persuade (talk to somebody and make him or her do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A dozen of residents were trapped in a burning building in the south eastern US state of Georgia. Firefighters set up ladders so that the people could escape the flames. As they climbed down the ladder, one of them dropped a child. Luckily, a firefighter safely caught the child. Difficult words: dozen (twelve), resident (a person who resides – lives somewhere), trapped (not able to escape – run away). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A building in Georgia, USA, caught fire. Twelve residents were trapped in the building. Firefighters set up ladders so that the people could get away. As they moved down a ladder, one of them dropped a child. Luckily, a firefighter safely caught the child. Difficult words: resident (a person who resides – lives somewhere), trapped (not able to escape – run away), ladder (a set of ‘stairs’ which you can move). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A building in the USA catches fire. Twelve people are in the building. Firefighters set up ladders . People can get away on them. The people move down a ladder. One person drops a child. Luckily, a firefighter catches the child. Difficult words: ladder (a set of ‘stairs’ which you can move), drop (let fall down). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Jakarta, a mezzanine floor inside the Indonesia Stock Exchange tower collapsed, and CCTV video showed about 30 students plunging into the lobby. Police said that although there were about 80 injuries, there were no fatalities . Police evacuated and cordoned off that area of the building, but trading resumed in the other areas. Authorities said that the collapse was not due to a militant attack. Difficult words: mezzanine (a small floor between other floors that is usually a balcony), fatality (death), cordon off (block off). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Jakarta, a mezzanine floor inside the Indonesia Stock Exchange tower collapsed. About 30 students plunged into the lobby. Police said that there were about 80 injuries but no deaths. Police evacuated and cordoned off the area of the building while trading resumed in the other areas. Leaders say that the floor did not fall because of a militant attack. Difficult words: mezzanine (a small floor between other floors that is usually a balcony), plunge (fall quickly), cordon off (block off). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Jakarta, there is a tower for the Indonesia Stock Exchange . It has a floor that is like a balcony. It is between the first and second floors. Video records that floor collapsing . About 30 students fall down to the floor below. The police say that 80 people get hurt. However, nobody dies. The police block off that part of the building. People can work in the other parts. Leaders say that militants did not make the floor fall. Difficult words: stock exchange (where people sell and trade stocks – parts of businesses), collapse (fall suddenly), militant (an extreme or violent person). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The world’s longest and fastest urban zip line has opened above Dubai’s marina . Starting at 168 metres from one of the buildings, you can reach speeds of up to 80 kilometres an hour. The zip line’s length is almost one kilometre. Difficult words: urban (in a city), marina (a safe place for people’s yachts and small boats). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Dubai, a new zip line opened. It is the longest and fastest urban zip line in the world. It starts at 168 metres above the city marina . You can go up to 80 kilometres an hour, as the zip line is almost one kilometre long. Difficult words: zip line (a cable between two places, down which you can go down for fun), urban (in a city), marina (a safe place for people’s yachts and small boats). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A new zip line opens in Dubai. It is the longest urban zip line in the world. It is one kilometre long. The zip line starts at 168 metres above the ground. It goes across the Dubai marina . You can go up to 80 kilometres an hour. Difficult words: zip line (a cable between two places that you can ride on for fun), urban (in a city), marina (a safe place for people’s yachts and small boats). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Chelsea Manning was an intelligence analyst for the US army who infamously leaked over 700,000 classified documents, and she served seven years out of a 35-year-sentence. Recently, she filed her statement of candidacy to run for the US senate in the state of Maryland where she will challenge Senator Ben Cardin. The 30-year-old hopes that her past will not hamper her plans. Difficult words: intelligence analyst (a person who analyses information to determine what might happen in the future), infamous (be famous for a negative reason), statement of candidacy (when a person announces that he or she will run for a political position), hamper (slow or stop). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Chelsea Manning was an intelligence analyst for the US army who leaked over 700,000 secret documents. She served 7 out of 35 years in jail. Recently, she filed her statement of candidacy to run for the US senate in the state of Maryland. She hopes that her past will not stop her plans. Difficult words: intelligence analyst (a person who analyses information to find out what can happen in the future), leak (reveal information), statement of candidacy (when a person says that he or she will run for a political position). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Chelsea Manning works for the US army. She is an intelligence analyst . She shows over 700,000 documents to the public. She is not supposed to do this. She can go to jail for 35 years. She goes to jail for 7 years. Now she wants to work in the US senate . She wants to be a politician . She hopes that her past does not stop her. Difficult words: intelligence analyst (a person who tries to find out what can happen in the future), senate (a part of the government where leaders make decisions for their states), politician (a leader in the government). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A meteoroid is a small body moving in the solar system, and when it enters the earth’s atmosphere, we call it a meteor. One meteor recently lit up the night sky across southern Michigan, a state in the northern USA. Reportedly ,it sent homes shaking too. An astronomer explained that as a meteor moves in the atmosphere, it compresses the gases in front of it. The gasses heat up and the meteor vaporises , producing light and noise. Difficult words: body (a piece of something), reportedly (according to what has been reported – said), compress (make much smaller), vaporise (turn into vapour – gas). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A meteoroid is a small body moving in the solar system, and when it enters the earth’s atmosphere, people call it a meteor. Recently, people saw a meteor in Michigan, a state in the northern USA. The meteor lit up the night sky, and people say that houses were shaking, too. As a meteor moves in the atmosphere, it compresses the gases in front of it. The gasses are heated up and the meteor vaporises . Light and noise can be produced, too. Difficult words: body (a piece of something), compress (make smaller), vaporise (turn into vapour – gas) You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Sometimes something small moves in the solar system . We call it a meteoroid. If it moves in Earth ’s atmosphere , we call it a meteor. People from Michigan, USA see a meteor. The meteor lights up the night sky. People say that houses shake, too. Difficult words: solar system (the sun and its 8 plants), Earth (‘our’ planet), atmosphere (the gasses/air around earth). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A dog named Jessie has been trained to smell for ink on banknotes. In just five months working at Heathrow, an international airport in London, she has sniffed out over £1 million in smuggled cash. She once discovered a haul of £350,000 in freight that was going abroad. Her handler calls her a ‘wonder dog’ and said that she knows she will only get her ball after she finds something, so she is motivated to work. Difficult words: sniff out (discover, find), smuggle (move something illegally abroad), haul (a quantity of something illegal), freight (in transport as things – not transported with a person). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A dog named Jessie was trained to smell for ink on banknotes which means that she can find money by smell. The dog works at Heathrow, an international airport in London. In just 5 months of work, she found £1 million in smuggled cash. Once, she discovered a haul of £350,000 in freight . The dog’s handler calls her a ‘wonder dog’. Difficult words: smuggle (transport illegally), haul (a quantity of something illegal), freight (in transport as things – not transported with a person). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about a dog. Her name is Jessie. She is trained to smell ink on banknotes . This means that she can find cash. The dog works at Heathrow Airport. It is an international airport in London. In 5 months, Jessie finds £1 million in smuggled cash. One day, she finds £350,000. Her handler calls her a ‘ wonder dog’. Difficult words: banknotes (paper money), smuggle (move illegally), handler (a person who trains and takes care of the dog), wonder (amazing, very great). Gale-force winds battered Europe on Thursday, killing several people. Falling trees killed two elderly men in the Netherlands, more than three people died in Germany, and one woman died in Belgium.
